html:
The Ikolen, better known as the Gavião of Rondônia, are an Indigenous people of western Brazil, living near Ji-Paraná in the state of Rondônia.

They speak a Mondé language of the Tupi family, related to those of the Paiter Suruí, the Zoró and the Cinta Larga. Rubber tappers and later settlers along the road into Rondônia brought them into contact with outsiders in the 1900s. Today they share the Igarapé Lourdes Indigenous Territory with the Arara (Karo) people.
